band_rationale: Normal = monthly moves of up to 2% in the smoothed series, the noise floor of claims data; fast = 5% or more month on month, sustained. Between is `emerging`.

definition: Month-on-month change in the three-month moving average of new initial unemployment claims from high-AI-exposure occupations in California (potential-exposure measure), from the California Policy Lab and EDD tracker.
name: California unemployment claims from AI-exposed occupations

status_events.author: claude-initial-seed
status_events.reason: California AI-Unemployment Tracker, July 2026 data (California Policy Lab; identical release on the EDD site): the 3-month moving average of high-AI-exposure initial claims rose about 1.0% month on month (52,300 to 52,800). Inside the normal band (<=2%). Initial seed.

timing_rationale: Leading: new unemployment claims rise before employment and wage statistics reflect job losses.
tracker_interpretation: Claims from exposed occupations are drifting up about a percent a month, in line with California's overall labour market, not ahead of it.
why_it_matters: Administrative claims data, not a survey and not a profile scrape; the closest thing to a real-time separations signal.
